text:
riley: Heads up - partner PoC just reported duplicate side-effects when using our Python async SDK with function/tool calling + structured output. Emails sent twice.

riley: Quick repro attached from their sample app (async client, function_call='auto').

riley: ```py
# repro (very small)
from redwood import AsyncClient
import os, uuid, asyncio

client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

async def run():
    invocation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    resp = await client.chat.create(
        model='rwd-1-7b',
        messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Send welcome email to user@example.com'}],
        tools=[{
            'name': 'send_email',
            'parameters': {'to': 'string', 'subject': 'string', 'body': 'string'},
            'metadata': {'invocation_id': invocation_id},
            'returns': 'application/json'
        }],
        function_call='auto'
    )
    print('chat id', resp.id)

asyncio.run(run())
```

riley: Their network logs show two separate POSTs to /v1/chat.create with different request ids but identical tool metadata.invocation_id. Server produced two function_invoke events: request=x1 then request=x2.

riley: Logs: 
INFO 2026-03-05T09:11:22Z request=x1 decision=function_call send_email invocation_id=abc-123
INFO 2026-03-05T09:11:23Z request=x2 decision=function_call send_email invocation_id=abc-123

tara: Thanks for the repro. Do we know if the client retried the original request or if the server re-emitted the invocation? Any 5xx or connection resets?

nate: I looked at the SDK telemetry the PoC shared: no 401s, but the client library did a single high-level retry after a socket timeout on the response stream. It looks like the first request made it to runtime and triggered the tool, but the client timed out waiting for completion and retried. That explains two server-side invocations.

priya: Right. This is a classic at-most-once vs at-least-once situation. We should either ensure an idempotency key is respected server-side or avoid retrying after a function_call decision is returned.

riley: Two asks: (1) short-term: place a sample-app mitigation so partners can opt into client-side invocation_id; (2) longer-term: expose an HTTP header (x-invocation-id) or a top-level request id that server will use to dedupe tool invocations.

tara: For the short-term patch, can we add invocation_id to the tool metadata and teach the SDK to send it as x-invocation-id header automatically if present? Minimal and backward-compatible. We'll need tests.

nate: We also need to update retry policy: once a response includes a tool decision (function_call) the client should not perform automatic retry of the same user prompt unless explicitly configured. Add an opt-in 'allow_tool_call_retries' flag defaulting to False.

priya: Sounds good. I'll open an infra ticket to add server-side dedupe support keyed on header or body field. But that will take cycles. Meanwhile sample app + SDK mitigations will help.

riley: I'll prep a sample-app PR that adds invocation_id generation and documents disabling automatic retries in the README. Will include a quick note for partners.

tara: Great. Please include a small unit/integration test in SDK repo that asserts the client sends x-invocation-id when tool.metadata.invocation_id is present. Also add a log message when a retry is suppressed due to tool_call decision.

deploy-bot: created tracker ticket 10234 (sdk: toolcall idempotency - short term) and notified eng-runtime.

nate: One more thought: we should clarify typing/structured output guidance in the sample. Some partners were attempting to return raw emails (string) vs structured JSON and then downstream caller logic triggered twice. Add examples for returns='application/json' and parse expectations.

riley: Good call. I'll add a small schema example and link to the SDK docs.

priya: Thanks everyone. Prioritizing infra ticket + SDK PR in the sprint.

riley: I'll update here with PR links shortly.
